post_text:
Backward compatibility in schemas is a slow-motion suicide pact.

💀

Stop lying to yourself about "safe" migrations.

Most engineers obsess over zero-downtime by keeping old columns alive indefinitely.

They think they are mitigating risk.

In reality, they are building a graveyard of nullable fields and zombie logic.

I’ve seen "temporary" bridge columns survive three major version migrations.

By the time we tried to clean them up, the original intent was long forgotten.

The mapping logic became so brittle that a simple type change crashed five microservices.

Maintaining two versions of the truth is a debt that compounds at 100% interest.

If you don't have a hard date to drop the old schema, you don't have a migration.

You have a mess.

Most people stop thinking right here.

If you don't kill your legacy columns, they will eventually kill your system. 🔪
lesson_extracted: Perpetual backward compatibility in database schemas creates unmanageable technical debt that eventually causes catastrophic system failure.
